title: Section 24 HMA — Maintenance pendente lite and expenses of proceedings

content.overview: Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 is maintenance pendente lite and expenses of the proceeding. In any proceeding under the Act, if it appears that either the wife or the husband has no independent income sufficient for support and the necessary expenses of the proceeding, the court may, on that party's application, order the respondent to pay the expenses of the proceeding and a monthly sum during the proceeding. The sum has regard to the petitioner's own income and the income of the respondent. The proviso says the application shall, as far as possible, be disposed of within sixty days from service of notice. The order lasts for the proceeding. It is not permanent alimony under section 25.
content.study: Either spouse may apply. The test is insufficient independent income for support and proceeding expenses. Fix the monthly sum against both incomes. Do not carry the order beyond the proceeding.

learningObjectives: State who may seek section 24 relief.
Tie the sum to both parties' incomes.
Separate pendente lite maintenance from section 25.
enhancement.definition: Section 24 is an interim order, in a proceeding under the Act, for expenses and monthly support where the applicant lacks sufficient independent income.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: The power is available to either spouse and only for the proceeding. It does not decide permanent alimony.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, section 24. Section 25 is permanent alimony.
essentialIngredients: No independent income sufficient for support and the necessary expenses
Respondent ordered to pay expenses and a monthly sum
Regard to the petitioner's income and the respondent's income
Disposal as far as possible within sixty days of service
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 24 is gender-neutral in terms. The applicant shows lack of independent income sufficient for personal support and for the necessary expenses of the proceeding. The court may order the respondent to pay those expenses and, monthly during the proceeding, such sum as seems reasonable having regard to both incomes. The proviso directs disposal, as far as possible, within sixty days from service of notice on the other spouse. The order is pendente lite. When the proceeding ends, permanent support is a section 25 question, decided on the wider factors in that section. A section 24 order does not prove the main relief.
examples: A wife with no independent income applies in a section 13 petition. The court may order expenses and a monthly sum having regard to both incomes.
A husband who lacks sufficient independent income applies against the wife. Section 24 does not confine the application to the wife.
The divorce petition is dismissed. The section 24 order does not continue as permanent alimony.
enhancement.problemApplication: Identify the pending proceeding, the applicant's independent income, and both incomes. Keep the order inside the proceeding and the sixty-day proviso as a disposal direction.
distinctions: Section 24 pendente lite vs section 25 permanent alimony
Either spouse vs a wife-only reading
Expenses of the proceeding vs monthly support
Sixty-day disposal direction vs a decision on the main petition
